guide.title: When the Northern Lamps Went Dark
guide.description: A continuous history of the Scourge crisis, Arthas's fall, the Legion's return, the defense of Mount Hyjal, and the road through Outland to the Frozen Throne.

nodes.title: The defeated inherit another beginning
nodes.narration: The Second War ended at a broken gate, yet its consequences endured in camps, ruined houses, and children raised beneath another people's watch. From among the interned orcs, Thrall gathered those willing to seek a future unlike the Old Horde's conquest. Liberation did not erase the blood behind them. It opened a harder question: what might a people become when the purpose imposed upon them was no longer their only road?

nodes.title: A quiet corruption enters the granaries
nodes.narration: While one people broke the locks of an older defeat, Lordaeron trusted in walls, harvests, and the familiar duties of peace. Into that ordered country came a plague whose first victories did not announce themselves with banners. Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned prepared the way; the Scourge grew where ordinary life had been made its instrument. Arthas and Jaina rode into a crisis whose true command still lay beyond their sight.

nodes.title: At Stratholme, purpose hardens into ruin
nodes.narration: At Stratholme, fear of what the infected might become narrowed Arthas's answer until no mercy remained within it. He ordered the city purged. Jaina and Uther would not follow that road, and the prince passed onward without them. The city stands here as an approximate light upon the atlas, for the deeper boundary crossed that day was not a city wall. It lay within the man who believed every cost could be justified by pursuit.

nodes.title: The hunter follows winter into the north
nodes.narration: Arthas carried his pursuit over the cold sea to Northrend. The route shown is only the shape of obsession across the world, not a chart of every landing and march. There he claimed Frostmourne, seeking the strength to defeat the enemy before him. The blade answered that desire by binding him to a greater enemy's will. He had ridden north to save Lordaeron; the man who turned homeward would become the kingdom's destroyer.

nodes.title: The prince returns beneath a colder allegiance
nodes.narration: The gates of Lordaeron opened to a returning prince and received a servant of the Lich King. Arthas killed his father, and the Scourge passed through the old kingdom's heart. A realm that had survived the Horde's northern war fell through the son it had trusted to defend it. The advance drawn across the map is broad and interpretive, because the catastrophe was larger than one army line: government, memory, and the safety of the living all gave way together.

nodes.title: The northern light is broken
nodes.narration: The Scourge turned next upon Quel'Thalas. Sylvanas resisted the advance and was answered with a captivity beyond death. The kingdom was broken, and the Sunwell corrupted as the invaders pursued a design reaching farther still. This passage must hold two truths together: a people suffered devastation, and one defender's transformation would later help create a power the Scourge could not wholly command. Ruin had begun to divide even the army of the dead.

nodes.title: The hand behind the dead steps through
nodes.narration: The Scourge had not been raised for conquest alone. Through the devastation of the north, the way opened for Archimonde and the Burning Legion to enter Azeroth once more. Kingdoms had been made into preparation; the undead host became the road by which an older enemy returned. Yet the Legion's victory in the east did not complete its purpose. Far across the sea stood Kalimdor, Mount Hyjal, and Nordrassil—the next height toward which the invasion bent.

nodes.title: A warning sends the New Horde beyond the sunset
nodes.narration: Warned that a greater darkness was coming, Thrall led the New Horde westward. The sea passage shown here is a narrative direction, not a captain's measured chart. Across it moved a people seeking ground on which a different future might stand, even while old violence traveled within them. Kalimdor offered no empty refuge. It held ancient guardians, unfamiliar powers, and conflicts that would test whether the new name could survive the habits of the old.

nodes.title: The old corruption demands one final answer
nodes.narration: Mannoroth's shadow still reached into orcish history. Grom fell again beneath that power, then stood with Thrall against the pit lord who embodied it. He died in the blow that broke the immediate demonic bond over their people. Liberation did not make the past harmless, nor did sacrifice settle every debt. It did remove one chain at the hour when the New Horde would need to choose whether it could stand beside others against the master that chain had served.

nodes.title: Three histories gather beneath one mountain
nodes.narration: Night elves, New Horde forces, and Alliance survivors did not arrive at Hyjal emptied of suspicion. Each carried losses, loyalties, and reasons to mistrust the others. The Legion gave them a danger none could outlast alone. Their coalition was temporary, and the atlas names it as such. Its meaning lies not in pretending difference vanished, but in showing that distinct peoples accepted one defense when the survival of every road behind them depended upon the mountain ahead.

nodes.title: At the World Tree, time becomes the defenders' weapon
nodes.narration: The defense yielded ground in order to purchase time. Archimonde climbed toward Nordrassil, believing the height already won. Then Malfurion called upon the power gathered around the World Tree, and the Legion commander was destroyed. The mountain survived, but victory was no return to the morning before the plague. Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas remained broken, the alliance at Hyjal would not become a single people, and the long-lived kaldorei paid a consequence of their own.

nodes.title: In fallen Lordaeron, the dead claim their own will
nodes.narration: Archimonde's defeat changed the balance far from Hyjal. As the Lich King's control weakened, Sylvanas and other undead broke free and made a place among Lordaeron's ruins. They named themselves the Forsaken. Freedom did not restore their lives or make the broken kingdom whole. It created another claimant to its future—born from the Scourge's cruelty, opposed to its mastery, and destined to complicate every simple division between the living and the dead.

nodes.title: Exile crosses into a world already broken
nodes.narration: Illidan's path led beyond Azeroth into Outland, where every horizon bore the memory of Draenor's ruin. With Kael'thas, Lady Vashj, and their followers, he closed portals and overthrew Magtheridon's rule. This was not the founding of a peaceful realm. It was the making of a stronghold by an uneasy coalition, shown within Outland's own local atlas. No line joins it falsely to Azeroth; the change of worlds is a change of map and measure.

nodes.title: Two purposes narrow toward the throne
nodes.narration: From Outland the story returns to Azeroth without pretending the worlds share one road. Illidan came to destroy the Frozen Throne; Arthas hastened north to preserve the power that had claimed him. Around Icecrown, the long histories of plague, exile, and demonic command drew into one contest. The route is a compact diagram of convergence, not a reconstruction of every campaign path. At its end, Illidan fell before he could reach the throne.

nodes.title: The lost prince ascends into a colder age
nodes.narration: Arthas climbed the Frozen Throne and joined his fate to the Lich King's power. The prince who had pursued the plague in hope of saving Lordaeron now ruled from the winter above the world he helped to break. Yet history did not end beneath that crown. The New Horde, the Forsaken, the survivors of kingdoms, and the peoples joined at Hyjal all carried changed inheritances forward. Beyond this threshold begins the age when adventurers would enter those wounds themselves.
